Chinese commentators see a political plot behind the Jensen Huang extramarital affair scandal

Chinese commentators suggest that Jensen Huang’s advocacy for continued access to the Chinese market, and his criticism of US chip restrictions may have made him a target of greater scrutiny.

Sana Hashmi

11 November, 2026 08:30 am IST

A headline on the Chinese news website Guancha declared that “The hunt for Nvidia is beginning to close in.” It captures a growing narrative in Chinese commentary that the controversy over Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s extramarital affair with Alice Huang is being used by Washington and Wall Street to increase pressure on the chipmaker.

A viral Weibo post highlighted Alice Huang’s career at Chinese state broadcasters Hunan TV and CCTV News , HSBC Private Bank and CITIC Securities, before she became managing director of Singapore-based Megaspeed in 2023. Claims that she had links to China and used her relationship with Huang to obtain chip-related information and circumvent export controls have been dismissed on Chinese internet as unsubstantiated .

The affair sparked intense debate across the Chinese internet since 30 October , before Jensen Huang’s public apology to his wife, in which he confessed to cheating. Discussion has ranged from national security and Huang’s private life to Nvidia’s future. On Weibo, there are hashtags about Huang admitting to infidelity, along with views that his confession was addressed to Capitol Hill.

Show Full Article

Beyond Huang’s private life For most Chinese commentators, the controversy has moved well beyond Huang’s personal reputation. Jin Yan , a special contributor to Caijing Magazine , argued that Huang’s personal relationships now raise questions about national security, export controls, and the consequences could extend across the entire AI supply chain.

A Baijiahao commentary makes a similar distinction: the focus, it argues, is on reports of foreign intelligence targeting Huang, rather than his infidelity.

Others have focused on what the scandal reveals about Nvidia itself. A Weibo post argued that while Huang’s infidelity is a personal moral issue, it also exposes the company’s dependence on its founder. After three decades under his leadership, Nvidia has no publicly announced succession plan, with little indication that Huang intends to step down. The post suggests that Huang’s growing geopolitical exposure could prompt investors to reassess key-person risk and its implications for the company’s valuation.

Shen Yi, a professor of international politics at Fudan University, placed the controversy surrounding Huang within the broader United States-China technology competition. He argued that Nvidia faces a security challenge shaped by competing approaches in Washington. Democrats may seek to curb AI expansion through regulation, while Republicans focus on national security and technology controls. Although their methods differ, both approaches could constrain American technology companies.

This, according to Shen, exposes a broader contradiction in US policy: Washington wants to maintain American dominance in AI while restricting China’s access to advanced computing, even as US companies and investors have strong commercial incentives to pursue opportunities in the Chinese market.

Espionage claims and the China factor In Chinese commentary, the espionage allegations are viewed largely through the lens of US-China rivalry. Some see them as another way for Washington to put pressure on a US technology company with deep commercial interests in China.

One analysis argued that American media have distorted the story to promote a broader anti-China narrative. It points to the portrayal of Huang’s association with an Asian woman as a potential intelligence link, and his calls for easing chip restrictions as evidence of Chinese influence.

The author suggests that Huang’s ‘Chinese’ heritage and position on the Chinese market have made him a target of US hawks. The allegations, the analysis argued, are intended to pressure Silicon Valley, stoke security fears and undermine prospects for improved US-China relations.

Other Chinese commentators focus on what the allegations could mean for Nvidia, regardless of whether espionage is established. Chinese publication World Science Pioneer said that media reports linking the controversy to foreign intelligence and national security risks have attracted much of the attention. Even if an investigation finds no leakage of trade secrets, the episode could still lead US regulators, customers and business partners to impose stricter requirements on information security, conflict-of-interest reviews and external communications.

A commentator pointed to bipartisan agreement in Washington on preventing advanced computing power from secretly reaching China.

Another Baijiahao commentary sees the scrutiny of Nvidia as following a familiar US political playbook: first accusations of chip transshipment, now allegations of intelligence links.

“The goals may change, but the script remains the same,” it said, drawing parallels with the earlier targeting of Huawei.

The author argued that as China narrows the US technological lead in AI, Washington is increasingly using political pressure to obstruct its rival, reflecting anxiety about its own technological competitiveness.

The message to Nvidia, it concludes, is clear: “If you obediently follow orders and cut off ties with China, then we’ll let you off the hook.”

Why now? The politics behind the timing For some Chinese commentators, the timing of the espionage controversy is important. They see it against the backdrop of Washington’s shifting approach to semiconductor exports and the continuing struggle over China’s access to advanced chips.

One commentary argued that Nvidia is caught between selective easing of chip export restrictions to China and continued scrutiny of its compliance with export controls. Huang has repeatedly criticised US restrictions, arguing that they undermine American competitiveness and push China to accelerate its own technological development.

Huang’s public support for open-weight AI models, including Chinese models, has also put him at odds with Washington’s more hawkish approach. Against this backdrop, the Chinese commentator questions why the allegations have surfaced now, suggesting they reflect wider geopolitical tensions over Nvidia’s continued business ties with China.

Another comment takes the argument further. It suggests that linking Huang’s personal scandal to allegations of Chinese espionage serves several political objectives: weakening his influence in Washington, discouraging Silicon Valley executives from advocating a softer approach toward China, providing justification for tighter chip export controls, and reinforcing the China threat narrative ahead of a new Congress.

Not all the commentary sees the controversy as an attempt to damage Nvidia itself.

A Weibo post said that new Democrat lawmakers could use the affair to warn other major technology companies that corporate misconduct carries consequences, without necessarily seeking to undermine Nvidia.

Writing for Guancha , Li Limeng offered a broader interpretation, presenting the controversy as part of a struggle for control of the US AI industry. In this account, Democrat establishment elites are seeking to consolidate their influence over AI models, energy infrastructure and semiconductor production through political networks, corporate appointments and governance mechanisms.

Also read: India is not an ally on demand. Its foreign policy must answer to its own people

A personal scandal with wider consequences Chinese reactions to the affair are far from uniform. They range from concerns about corporate governance and national security to claims of political manoeuvring in Washington. Yet a recurring theme is that the controversy cannot be separated from the wider US-China technology rivalry.

Some commentators suggest that Huang’s advocacy for continued access to the Chinese market, and his criticism of US chip restrictions, may have made him a target of greater scrutiny. They suspect that Huang’s personal relationships are now being used against him and viewed through the lens of national security.

Some see the affair as a means of putting pressure on Huang and Nvidia, while narrowing the space for US-China technology cooperation. Others believe its consequences could extend beyond the company, affecting the rules governing technology leaders and the direction of the global AI industry. In this reading, what began as a personal scandal involving one of the world’s most prominent technology executives has become part of a much larger debate about the future of AI and the intensifying US-China rivalry.

Sana Hashmi, PhD, is a fellow at the Taiwan-Asia Exchange Foundation and George HW Bush Foundation for US-China Relations. She tweets @sanahashmi1. Views are personal.

(Edited by Ratan Priya)

By Joshua McElwee BUENOS AIRES, Argentina, Nov 10 (Reuters) – Pope Leo drew a crowd of a million on Tuesday for the third strong turnout of his 12-day South America tour, as he urged young people at a nighttime vigil in Argentina not to be consumed by the pursuit of money or social media popularity.

Throngs stretched for miles down the Avenida del Libertador, one of Buenos Aires’ main boulevards. Many waved cell phones, screens shining in the black night, as Leo was driven slowly through the crowd in an open-air popemobile.

Chants of “This is the pope’s youth!” rang out as the vehicle stopped frequently so security officials could bring forward babies for Leo to bless.

Show Full Article

In a speech, the pope warned young people against worship of modern-day “idols” such as success or physical appearance, and lamented that some youth “go so far as to lie, betray or humiliate someone on social media.”

“Do not bow down before anything that cannot give you life,” he said.

Leo, on an ambitious three-country tour through November 17, led the vigil after returning from a day trip to Cordoba, Argentina’s second city, where he drew 650,000 people to an outdoor Mass earlier on Tuesday.

The pope led a Mass on Monday at the Avenida del Libertador that drew 2.5 million people, in the largest event of his 18-month-old papacy.

POPE SEEKS TO SHORE UP CATHOLIC STRONGHOLD

Leo is the first pope to visit Catholic-majority Argentina since 1987.

The pope, who is also visiting Uruguay and Peru on the tour, is seeking to reinforce a region that has long been a Catholic stronghold but where the Church has been losing ground to fast-growing evangelical denominations.

Leo has emerged as a forceful voice on the world stage, lamenting what he sees as a failure of global leadership. In Argentina, he has directly challenged President Javier Milei, a libertarian and close ally of US President Donald Trump.

On Sunday, Leo urged Milei, who has pushed an austerity agenda that the Church has criticized for cutting social services, not to target Argentina’s poorest. Milei has said spending cuts were necessary to bring inflation under control.

Valentin Gomez, 21, a student attending the Mass in Cordoba, praised Leo’s focus on those in need.

“In these difficult times we are living through, he is greatly needed,” Gomez said. “Someone who is truly concerned about the poor.”

Cordoba Cardinal Angel Sixto Rossi, a critic of the austerity policies, welcomed Leo’s visit as a chance for the pope to see how Argentina is suffering under Milei’s measures.

“He knows how beautiful our people are and the ugly part, the leadership of the government,” he said in an interview with Argentine media. “He doesn’t arrive blindfolded.”

Argentine Foreign Minister Pablo Quirno said Cordoba was chosen as a stop on the pope’s tour because of its location in the center of Argentina, allowing pilgrims to travel easily from neighboring provinces.

Leo, the first US-born pope, spent decades as a missionary in Peru. The Vatican has described the trip, one of the most demanding foreign tours by a pope in decades, as a “homecoming” for him.

(Reporting by Joshua McElwee, additional reporting by Leila Miller, Lucila Sigal, Horacio Soria; editing by Chizu Nomiyama, Rod Nickel and Stephen Coates)

WASHINGTON, Nov 10 (Reuters) – US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent recently moved out of his home and onto a military base after Iranian threats against his life, the New York Times reported on Tuesday, citing sources with knowledge of the matter.

Iran has ramped up efforts to target US personnel, and lethal plots by Tehran against American citizens have reached “advanced stages”, a senior intelligence official in the Trump administration warned in a memo seen by Reuters late last month.

The newspaper reported that the severity of the threats to Bessent was not immediately clear.

Show Full Article

Iran has previously denied plotting to attack officials and people on US soil.

The newspaper reported that US officials have noted that Iran’s ability to carry out large-scale attacks in the US and other territories overseas is limited.

The US Treasury Department did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Bessent has been the face of Washington’s economic pressure campaign against Tehran during the course of the US-Israeli war on Iran that began on February 28.

US-Israeli strikes on Iran and Israeli attacks on Lebanon during the war have killed thousands and displaced millions.

American and Israeli attacks have also killed top Iranian officials, including late Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

(Reporting by Kanishka Singh in Washington; editing by Michelle Nichols )

Nov 11 (Reuters) – Russia shot down 92 drones early on Wednesday in an attack over the Leningrad region northwest of Moscow, Governor Aleksandr Drozdenko said on the Telegram messaging app.

The region is home to the ports of Ust-Luga, Primorsk and Vysotsk, key for Russia’s oil and grain exports on the Baltic Sea, as well as the Kirishi oil refinery, Russia’s second-largest.

Reuters could not immediately independently confirm the report.

Show Full Article

On Monday, a drone struck the Kirishi refinery, run by Surgutneftegaz, setting the plant on fire, and killed a woman in the region where St Petersburg, the hometown of President Vladimir Putin, is located.

Neighbours Latvia and Lithuania warned people to seek shelter against the threats of unidentified drones entering their airspace via Russia or Belarus, and said NATO air defence fighter jets were activated.

In Ukraine, power went out in part of the central city of Kryvyi Rih, an industrial stronghold and hometown of President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, after a drone attack, an official said on Telegram.

The attacks come as the United States attempts a new peace push at the first Russia-Ukraine talks in nine months in Abu Dhabi, set to continue on Wednesday.

(Reporting by Georgina McCartney in Houston;Editing by Jekaterīna Golubkova and Clarence Fernandez)
